title: Steering escape hunt notes (multizone)
content:
Goal: quick, scribbly log of the multizone steering/escape incidents that started 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC. Use this to hand off to SRE and the steering policy owners. Rough. TODOs at the end.

Symptoms observed
- Several customer requests (hosted API) took a long tail of latency and then returned model-mismatch errors (client saw different model id than requested) or 502 from the edge.
- Spike in regional ejection events from steering controller: east-us-1 -> zone ejected at 03:12:15, 03:15:01, 03:17:44 (bursty).
- Autoscaling did not trigger immediate additional dedicated capacity for several minutes; requests were routed to fallback region (eu-west-1) with higher RTT and occasional tokenization errors.
- Alert flood: steering-controller rate-limit counter increased; many controller-sync warnings: "policy_election_delay: >5s"

What I ran (commands, rough outputs)
- kubectl -n inference logs steering-controller-5c7bbf8 | grep -i ejected --context=2
  -> saw repeated messages: "EjectCandidate(zone=east-us-1, reason=latency_surge, policy_version=2.14)"
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood/redwood/v1/requests?trace=1" | jq '.routes'
  -> route chosen: "eu-west-1-fallback" for requests originally pinned to east-us-1 because controller returned route_score below threshold.
- tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/steer.pcap (30s capture) -> saw TCP retransmits to east-us-1 at 03:12:16-03:12:19, but SYN/ACKs returned later from eu-west-1.
- grep -R "kv-cache-mismatch" /var/log/inference/* -> zero hits (so not obviously KV mismatch while serving)
- redis-cli -h routing-cache info -> no memory alarms, TTL churn normal (avg TTLs 45s)

Interesting log snippets (copied raw)
- steering-controller: WARN policy_election_delay_ms=5023 zone=east-us-1 candidates=3 details="backoff window exceeded"
- edge-proxy: ERROR upstream-502 zone=eu-west-1 code=502 body="Upstream returned invalid stream token"
- serving-agent[east-us-1]: WARN model-pin-mismatch request_id=abc123 requested=v1.9.0 served=v1.8.3

Hypotheses (brain dump)
1) Controller election/backoff bug: policy_election_delay indicates the controller couldn't reach required quorum or took too long; maybe the policy store (consul/etcd) had a transient partition causing stale policy_version to be used. That could explain repeated re-ejections and inconsistent model pins.
2) Cache TTL + steering heartbeat drift: if steering heartbeats are >TTL we might falsely consider nodes unhealthy and elect fallback routes too aggressively. Observed TTLs ~45s and some controller delays ~5s — borderline but not fatal normally. Something else increased latency (network queueing) causing cascading ejections.
3) Tokenization/model mismatch on fallback path: fallback region uses a slightly different runtime binary/quantization leading to tokenization differences -> client sees model id mismatch or invalid token streams -> 502. Check build tags and quant profiles across regions.
4) Route scoring anomaly: route_score function contains a factor that multiplies recent errors; a burst of transient errors from a noisy instance could drop the whole zone below threshold. If policy_version=2.14 introduced a more aggressive penalty, that would match timing.

Immediate checks to validate hypotheses
- Check policy store metrics (etcd/consul) around 03:10-03:20 UTC: api latency, leader changes.
- Compare steering-controller binary versions/election library versions across zones. Any rollout? PRs? (linked GH PRs above).
- Cross-compare runtime build tags: curl to /metadata endpoint on a sample node in east-us-1 and eu-west-1; check quantization profile and model hashes.
- Re-run a controlled load test against east-us-1 to reproduce route_score drop: use replay of failing request samples with tracing header to force deterministic scoring.

Repro steps (manual)
1) From devbox, set trace header X-RW-TRACE=steer-debug and send 50 requests with same prompt -> watch steering-controller logs and route_score outputs.
2) If reproduces, capture metrics from /debug/route_score and /debug/policy_state endpoints.
3) If route_score dips, use git bisect on policy scoring function (branch: policy/main) between commits around 2 weeks ago.

Notes on mitigations applied (yesterday)
- Temporarily bumped route_score threshold on steering policy to make scoring less sensitive (manual override via console). That reduced ejections but increased tail latency for some customers.
- Scoped a hotfix to the controller to add extra logging around election timeouts (deployed to staging only).

Open questions / unknowns
- Did any infra network changes happen near 03:10 UTC? (cloud provider maintenance window?). I couldn't find provider maintenance in the portal but need NetEng to confirm.
- Do we have a consistent model version pin across regions for the small models (seq2seq v1)? Serving-agent reports mismatch — could be an older artifact in east-us-1 image cache.
- Were any autoscaler configs changed (min_replicas, burst limits) in the last day? Autoscaling slow reaction might be config-related.

Quick correlates I want (short commands to run, fill results here)
- etcdctl --endpoints=<policy-store> endpoint status --write-out table -> (fill)
- curl -s http://east-us-1-node/debug/metadata | jq .build_tags -> (fill)
- gcloud compute operations list --filter='region:(us-east1) AND startTime>2026-03-10T02:50:00Z' -> (fill)

Decisions / next actions
- Ask SRE to temporarily pin steering policy to previous stable version (2.13) for 1 hour to see if election/backoff behavior normalizes. (Ravi to coordinate).
- Patch: add a defensive check in route_score that requires at least N independent instance errors (avoid single noisy instance dropping whole zone). Quick patch PR drafted (GH:runtime/pull/987).
- Verify artifact pinning pipeline: ensure that region build promotion hasn't been skipped. If artifact mismatch found, trigger redeploy of correct model binary to east-us-1.

Notes to self (things I noticed)
- The model-pin-mismatch logs include a short hex suffix that looks like the image digest (v1.9.0+sha256:7f3a). The east-us nodes show older sha in /var/lib/serving/artifact.manifest.
- Some of the rejected requests have long prompt lengths (token counts > 4k) — maybe fallback runtime uses older tokenizer that fails on long input.

TODOs (short)
- [ ] Collect etcd/consul leader history from 03:00-03:30 UTC (SRE)
- [ ] Fetch build_tags and artifact manifests from a sample of nodes in east-us-1 and eu-west-1 (me)
- [ ] Run replay load with X-RW-TRACE header (Ravi)
- [ ] Confirm cloud provider network events (NetEng)
- [ ] If artifact mismatch, schedule urgent redeploy (Sasha)

If I get time later: instrument debug endpoints to emit last-5-route-scores in controller health payload so console can quickly show transient drops. That might make future hunts faster.

References / breadcrumbs
- Slack thread: #prod-routing (ts 1678542000.000200) -> initial alert and captures.
- JIRA: INF-3421 (investigate steering election delays)
- GH: runtime/pull/987 (patch for route_score resilience)

End of scratch. Will update with fills for the quick correlates above.
